capabilities: Export a Markdown pipe table as a UTF-8 CSV file
Preview CSV text with row and column counts before saving
Choose the field delimiter and omit or keep the header row
Add a UTF-8 byte order mark to the output file
Batch-export all tables in a folder with Pro
disambiguation: Not a table editor or formatter; it reads pipe tables and writes them out as CSV files without changing the note.
extras: Freemium: free single-table export has no quota; Pro folder batch needs a GitHub Sponsors payment checked via device-flow sign-in. The plugin opens a promotional 'What's new' tab after updates suggesting other NoteMods plugins and Zovo Chat; it sends no note content or telemetry.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to save a table from a note as an encoded CSV file, and non-ASCII text can be mangled by other export paths.

requires.name: GitHub Sponsors sponsorship of theluckystrike ($5/month or $15 once) for Pro batch export

summary: Exports Markdown pipe tables to UTF-8 CSV files with a preview, delimiter and BOM options, plus a Pro folder batch export.
